qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: While specialized clinical build-outs in outpatient medical buildings and lab installations create modest tenant switching costs, DOC fails proof of moat. 10-year historical GAAP ROIC is structurally ~4.5% (<12% hurdle), and pricing power is severely constrained by contractual 2.5-3.0% rent escalators alongside significant life-science lab space oversupply in core biotech clusters.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 4.5% < 12%, REJECT). Healthpeak operates capital-intensive healthcare real estate (outpatient medical clinics and life-science labs) with structural returns on capital well below the 12% Munger threshold. Modest contractual rent escalators (2.5-3%) lag long-term inflation and higher cost of capital, while post-pandemic lab oversupply in key hubs suppresses organic pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle ROIC median sits at ~4.5% (with recent 2024-2025 trailing ROIC between 1.5% and 3.5%), structurally constrained by capital-intensive property acquisition and development costs against 5.5-7.0% nominal cap rates. The all-stock merger of equals with Physicians Realty Trust in 2024 expanded outpatient medical building exposure to ~50% of the portfolio alongside lab space (~45%), but does not alter low un-levered capital efficiency. Outpatient medical leases feature fixed 2.5-3% annual escalators unable to outpace cost-of-capital inflation, while life science lab assets face ongoing vacancy and concession headwinds in South San Francisco, Boston, and San Diego.
